content.text:
**Observations**

*Dead vs. live inputs.* A large set of W1 rows are pure initialization noise (all 16 values within ±0.035, no sign coherence): row 0 of the image except columns 12–15; row 1 columns 0–3 and 24–27; row 2 columns 0–1 and 26–27; row 3 columns 0–1 and 27; rows 4–6 columns 0–1; row 26 columns 26–27; row 27 columns 0–3 and 24–27. Everything else has learned structure. So the pixels that are *never* lit form only small triangular corner regions plus (almost all of) the very top row; the live region is essentially the whole 28×28 frame, with the first row/column slightly "deader" than the last row/column.

*Where the biggest weights are.* The largest magnitudes (|w| ≈ 0.2–0.36) sit at the frame edges, not the center: image rows 1–2 across columns 4–26 (e.g. unit 15 +0.19…+0.36, units 6/10/5 −0.2…−0.35); the bottom row 27, columns 4–23, strongest at center columns 13–17 (unit 1 −0.35, unit 13 +0.34, unit 14 −0.25); the left edge at columns 1–3 for rows 6–12 (unit 13 +0.33 at (7,3), unit 1 −0.37 at (12,2)); the right edge at column 26 for rows 10–11 (unit 0 +0.35, unit 14 +0.29); and a central band at rows 9–11, columns 14–18 (units 2, 3, 13 ≈ +0.2…+0.29). Weights vary smoothly along a row and come in broad bands – silhouette/edge-of-blob structure rather than thin stroke templates.

*Hidden units.* Unit 15 ≈ "top of frame filled"; unit 6 and unit 10 ≈ "top of frame empty, content at mid-right/edges"; unit 1 ≈ "bottom row empty"; unit 13 ≈ "bottom-center filled and left edge filled at rows 6–8"; unit 0 responds to content at both left (col 2) and right (col 26) extremes; unit 14 has opposite signs at the left edge (−) and right edge (+) at rows 10–12, i.e. a left/right asymmetry detector. Unit 9 is negative wherever rows 9–10 are lit at columns 8–12 and 22–24 (sleeve/shoulder region) but positive for content at rows 3–5.

*Output layer.* W2 is dense and mixed-sign (|w| up to 1.8) – a distributed code, as expected for only 16 units. Unit 6 ("nothing at the top, stuff at the sides") votes +for classes 5, 7, 9 and 4, strongly − for class 1; unit 14 (asymmetry) votes + for 5 and 8, − for 7, 0, 2, 4; unit 13 votes + for 0, 2, 3, 7 and − for 4, 6, 8, 9.

**Reasoning**

- Exactly-zero background pixels (init-noise weights) ⇒ objects on a black background, not natural photographs (CIFAR-style grayscale would have no dead pixels).
- The live region fills the entire frame: rows 1–2 and row 27 and columns 0/27 carry the *strongest* weights. In MNIST (and EMNIST, KMNIST) the glyph sits in a ~20×20 box with ~4-pixel margins, so rows 0–3, 24–27 and columns 0–3, 24–27 would be dead or nearly so. That rules those out.
- Fashion-MNIST's preprocessing scales the longest edge of each item to 28 px and centers it: tall items (trousers, dresses, coats) touch the top and bottom rows; wide items (sandals, sneakers, boots, bags) touch columns 0 and 27 in the middle rows; the corners stay empty. That is exactly the live/dead map seen here, including the fact that the mid-row left/right columns light up only from row ~6 downward (shoe soles, sleeve tips) and the bottom row is lit broadly (hems, trouser legs). The slight off-by-one (row 0 and column 0 less used than row 27/column 27) is consistent with the subsampling-based resize.
- Broad band-like weights and detectors for "top filled vs. empty" (garments vs. footwear), "bottom row filled" (trousers/dresses vs. shoes/bags), left-edge sleeve tips, and especially a left/right asymmetry unit all make sense for Fashion-MNIST, where shoes all point the same way while garments are symmetric. notMNIST letters would light the whole top row; KMNIST/MNIST strokes would give thin, centered templates.

**Dataset:** Fashion-MNIST (Zalando clothing-article images, 28×28 grayscale, 10 classes, 60k/10k split).

**Classes:** 0 T-shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence:** 75%
